script:
Presenter: Hamad, you were helping with the school travel project, weren't you?
Hamad: Yes. We wanted to make it easier for students and visitors to understand local bus routes and safer ways to travel.
Presenter: Where did you get your information?
Hamad: We visited the transport information centre and spoke to the transport coordinator.
Presenter: Did you prepare anything for people to use?
Hamad: We made a route timetable with the main stops and travel details.
Presenter: How did you check that the information was correct?
Hamad: The coordinator checked it with us. We also compared it with the official transport notice.
Presenter: Did you have any problems while preparing it?
Hamad: Yes, one bus departure time had changed after we had printed the first version.
Presenter: That must have been frustrating. What did you do?
Hamad: We checked the new time, corrected the notice and made sure everyone had the updated copy.
Presenter: When was your training session?
Hamad: It was on Tuesday morning. We practised comparing routes and explaining the options clearly.
Presenter: Who was the guide for the session?
Hamad: The transport coordinator showed us how to check details and answer questions.
Presenter: Were all the visitors asking the same things?
Hamad: No. Some wanted the quickest route, while others needed information about accessible stops.
Presenter: How did you help someone who needed extra support?
Hamad: We asked what they needed instead of guessing, then explained the available choices.
Presenter: Did the group work together well?
Hamad: Yes. Some students researched routes, others prepared the timetable, and a few practised speaking to visitors.
Presenter: What happened after people gave you feedback?
Hamad: We wrote down their comments and improved the guide where the suggestions were useful.
Presenter: Will you continue the project?
Hamad: Next term, we want to make a practical travel information guide for the school.
Mariam: We also included a note showing where passengers could ask for extra help.
Presenter: What's the most important thing you learned?
Hamad: Travel information has to be accurate and easy to understand. A small mistake can make someone miss a bus.
